questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
options: Please wait a moment.
Please come a little closer.
Please speak a little more slowly.
Please wait outside.
questions.explanation: You heard 「ちょっと待ってください。」. ちょっと is 'a little' or 'a moment', and 待って is the て-form of 待つ, to wait; 'wait outside' would need 外で.

audio.text: ちょっと待ってください。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker saying?
options: Thank you for waiting for me.
Sorry to interrupt you.
Excuse me for leaving before you.
Please go ahead of me.
questions.explanation: You heard 「お先にしつれいします。」, said when leaving work or a club before others. お先にどうぞ, 'please go ahead', starts with the same words, so the ending is what has to be heard.

audio.text: お先にしつれいします。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the host saying?
options: Please go ahead and eat.
Please come inside.
Please sit down here.
Please take some home.
questions.explanation: You heard 「どうぞ、めしあがってください。」. めしあがる is the respectful verb for eating or drinking, used by a host to a guest.

audio.text: どうぞ、めしあがってください。

questions.stem: Listen, then choose the meaning.
options: You look well.
I hear you're well.
You don't look well.
Are you feeling well?
questions.explanation: You heard 「元気そうですね。」. A な-adjective plus そう gives appearance: 'you look well'. 'I hear you're well' would be the hearsay 元気だそうです.

audio.text: 元気そうですね。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
options: Where did you go?
What did you buy?
What's the matter?
What will you do?
questions.explanation: You heard 「どうしたんですか。」, asked when someone seems upset or unwell. The んですか ending asks for an explanation of something the speaker has noticed.

audio.text: どうしたんですか。

questions.stem: Listen. When would you say this?
options: When leaving your own home
When arriving back at your own home
When starting a meal
When entering someone's home
questions.explanation: You heard 「おじゃまします。」, literally 'I am going to intrude', said as a visitor steps into someone's home. Arriving back home is ただいま, and before a meal people say いただきます.

audio.text: おじゃまします。

questions.stem: Listen to Ken's phone message. What time does the film start?
questions.explanation: You heard 「六時じゃなくて、七時半に始まります」: 'not at six, it starts at half past seven'. Seven o'clock is when they will meet in front of the station.

audio.text: もしもし、ケンです。明日のえいがですが、六時じゃなくて、七時半に始まります。駅の前で七時に会いましょう。

questions.stem: Listen to the phone message. Why is the caller ringing?
options: The caller will be late for work today.
The caller cannot work tomorrow.
The caller would like more shifts at work.
The caller is sick and will miss work today.
questions.explanation: You heard 「かぜをひいたので、今日のアルバイトを休みます」: 'I've caught a cold, so I'll take today's shift off'. The caller says 明日は行きます, so tomorrow is fine.

audio.text: もしもし、田中です。すみません、かぜをひいたので、今日のアルバイトを休みます。明日は行きます。

questions.stem: Listen to the message. What does the speaker want?
options: To be picked up from the station by car
To be told the way home from the station
To borrow an umbrella at the station
To be met at the bus stop by car
questions.explanation: You heard 「車でむかえに来てくれる？」, 'will you come and get me by car?', after 駅に着いたよ, 'I've arrived at the station'. The rain is the reason, not a request for an umbrella.

audio.text: お母さん、私。今、駅に着いたよ。雨がふっているから、車でむかえに来てくれる？

questions.stem: Listen to Lisa's message to her teacher. Why will she be away?
options: She is going on a family trip.
She has a part-time job.
She has missed the bus.
She is going to the hospital.
questions.explanation: You heard 「今日は病院に行くので、学校を休みます」: 'I'm going to the hospital, so I'll be away from school today'. She also says she will hand in her homework tomorrow.

audio.text: 山田先生、二年生のリサです。今日は病院に行くので、学校を休みます。しゅくだいは明日出します。

questions.stem: Listen to the message from the hotel. How many nights has the guest booked?
options: Two
Three
Ten
Eight
questions.explanation: You heard 「八月十日から三泊」: three nights from 10 August. Eight is the month and ten the date, details placed to catch a careless listener.

audio.text: こちらはホテルさくらです。ごよやくは八月十日から三泊ですね。チェックインは午後三時からです。

questions.stem: Listen to Emma's message. What is she offering to do?
options: Have the party at her house
Come early to help with the cooking
Drive people home after the party
Bring something, such as drinks
questions.explanation: You heard 「何か持っていきましょうか。飲み物でもいいですよ」: 'Shall I bring something? Drinks would be fine'. 〜ましょうか here is an offer.

audio.text: もしもし、エマです。あさってのパーティー、私も行きます。何か持っていきましょうか。飲み物でもいいですよ。

questions.stem: Listen to the station announcement. What is happening?
options: A train from Kyoto has arrived at platform 3.
A train to Tokyo is arriving at platform 3.
A train to Kyoto has been cancelled.
A train to Kyoto is arriving at platform 3.
questions.explanation: You heard 「三番ホームに京都行きの電車がまいります」. 京都行き means 'bound for Kyoto', and まいります, the humble form of 来ます, is how stations announce a train that is about to arrive.

audio.text: まもなく、三番ホームに京都行きの電車がまいります。

questions.stem: Listen to the school announcement. What has happened to the sports day?
options: It has been cancelled because of the rain.
It has moved to this Friday because of rain.
It has moved to next Friday because of rain.
It will go ahead tomorrow despite the rain.
questions.explanation: You heard 「うんどう会は来週の金曜日になりました」, after 明日は雨がふるので. 来週 is next week, so it is next Friday, and になりました shows a change of date, not a cancellation.

audio.text: せいとのみなさん、明日は雨がふるので、うんどう会は来週の金曜日になりました。

questions.stem: Listen to the shop announcement. What is on special today?
options: Fruit only, 20 per cent off
All fruit and vegetables, 10 per cent off
All meat and fish, 20 per cent off
All fruit and vegetables, 20 per cent off
questions.explanation: You heard 「くだものとやさいがぜんぶ二十パーセント安くなっています」. ぜんぶ is 'all', and both fruit and vegetables are named.

audio.text: 今日は、くだものとやさいがぜんぶ二十パーセント安くなっています。

questions.stem: Listen to the library announcement. When is the library closed?
options: Every Friday
Every Monday
Every Sunday
Every Tuesday
questions.explanation: You heard 「毎週月曜日が休みです」: closed every Monday. It is open from Tuesday (火曜日) to Sunday (日曜日), 9 am to 5 pm.

audio.text: としょかんは毎週月曜日が休みです。火曜日から日曜日までは、午前九時から午後五時まであいています。

questions.stem: Listen to the airport announcement. What is the problem?
options: The flight to Sydney is an hour late because of a technical fault.
The flight to Sydney is an hour late because of bad weather.
The flight to Sydney is cancelled because of bad weather.
The flight from Sydney is an hour late because of bad weather.
questions.explanation: You heard 「シドニー行きのひこうきは、天気がわるいので、一時間おくれます」. 行き means 'bound for', so the flight is going to Sydney, and おくれます means it will be late, not cancelled.

audio.text: シドニー行きのひこうきは、天気がわるいので、一時間おくれます。

questions.stem: Listen to the weather forecast. What is forecast for tomorrow?
options: Rain in the morning, then fine from the afternoon
Rain all day, heavier in the afternoon
Fine all day, cooler in the afternoon
Fine in the morning, then rain from the afternoon
questions.explanation: You heard 「午前中ははれますが、午後から雨がふるでしょう」. 午前中 is the morning and 午後から 'from the afternoon'; が marks the change from fine weather to rain.

audio.text: 明日は、午前中ははれますが、午後から雨がふるでしょう。

questions.stem: Listen to the tour guide. Which statement is correct?
options: Photos are allowed inside the temple.
The souvenir shop is to the left of the exit.
The souvenir shop is next to the entrance.
Photos are not allowed inside the temple.
questions.explanation: You heard 「お寺の中では、しゃしんをとってはいけません」: photos must not be taken inside. The souvenir shop is 出口の右, to the right of the exit.

audio.text: みなさん、お寺の中では、しゃしんをとってはいけません。おみやげの店は出口の右にあります。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about manga and anime?
options: Watches anime every day after school
Loves manga but rarely watches anime
Loves anime but rarely reads manga
Loves both manga and anime equally
questions.explanation: You heard 「まんがは大好きですが、アニメはあまり見ません」. あまり with a negative verb means 'not much', and が marks the contrast between the two.

audio.text: 日本のまんがは大好きですが、アニメはあまり見ません。

questions.stem: Listen. Why does the speaker have a part-time job?
options: To save for a trip to Japan next year
Because the work is easy and fun
To save for a car next year
To pay for a trip to Japan this year
questions.explanation: You heard 「お金をためて、来年日本に旅行したいと思っています」. ためる is to save money, and 来年 is next year. The speaker says the job is たいへん, hard work.

audio.text: アルバイトはたいへんですが、お金をためて、来年日本に旅行したいと思っています。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's view of social media?
options: Inconvenient, and a waste of everyone's time
Convenient, and worth using as much as possible
Dangerous, so young people should not use it
Convenient, but using it too much is not good
questions.explanation: You heard 「べんりですが、使いすぎるのはよくないと思います」. Both halves matter: a positive view, then a limit on it introduced by が. 使いすぎる is 'to use too much'.

audio.text: ソーシャルメディアはべんりですが、使いすぎるのはよくないと思います。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to be, and why?
options: A high school teacher, from liking study
A primary school teacher, like their mother
A doctor, from wanting to help children
A primary school teacher, from liking children
questions.explanation: You heard 「小学校の先生になりたいです。子どもが好きだからです」. 小学校 is primary school, and 〜からです gives the reason.

audio.text: しょうらいは、小学校の先生になりたいです。子どもが好きだからです。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker eat more often now?
options: Vegetables
Meat and fish equally
Fish
Meat
questions.explanation: You heard 「前は肉が大好きでしたが、今は魚のほうがよく食べます」. 前は marks the past, 今は the present, and 魚のほう means 'fish, rather than the other'.

audio.text: 前は肉が大好きでしたが、今は魚のほうがよく食べます。

questions.stem: Listen. How is the speaker feeling?
options: Relieved that the test turned out easy
Pleased that the test has been cancelled
Bored, because the test is next week
Worried, not having known about the test
questions.explanation: You heard 「テストは明日？知らなかった！どうしよう」. 知らなかった is 'I didn't know', and どうしよう, 'what shall I do?', shows panic.

audio.text: えっ、テストは明日？知らなかった！どうしよう。

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?
options: Sad that the summer holidays are over
Worried about homework over the holidays
Tired after a long day at the beach
Happy the summer holidays have finally come
questions.explanation: You heard 「やっと夏休みだ！」. やっと means 'at last', and 毎日海に行って、のんびりしたい says what the speaker is looking forward to.

audio.text: やっと夏休みだ！毎日海に行って、のんびりしたいなあ。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker do, and why?
options: Takes their own bag shopping, to cut rubbish
Buys a new bag each time, to help the shop
Picks up rubbish in town every weekend
Shops less often, so as to save money
questions.explanation: You heard 「町のゴミをへらしたいので、買い物にはいつも自分のふくろを持っていきます」. へらす is to reduce, and 自分のふくろ is 'my own bag'.

audio.text: 町のゴミをへらしたいので、買い物にはいつも自分のふくろを持っていきます。

questions.stem: Listen. Why does the speaker often visit their grandfather?
options: He lives next door.
He has no phone.
He lives on his own.
He is in hospital.
questions.explanation: You heard 「そふも一人で住んでいるので、よく会いに行きます」. 一人で住んでいる is 'lives alone', and ので gives it as the reason; the first sentence is about Japan's ageing population in general.

audio.text: 日本では、お年よりが多くなっています。私のそふも一人で住んでいるので、よく会いに行きます。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker like about the app?
options: It translates English into Japanese.
It can be used without paying.
It shows how to read kanji straight away.
It teaches how to write kanji neatly.
questions.explanation: You heard 「漢字の読み方がすぐ分かるので、とてもべんりです」. 読み方 is 'how to read', and すぐ is 'straight away'.

audio.text: このアプリを使うと、漢字の読み方がすぐ分かるので、とてもべんりです。

questions.stem: Listen. Who is being spoken to, and what is the speaker doing?
options: A classmate; asking to borrow a pen
A teacher; asking permission to ask something
A friend; asking for help with homework
A teacher; asking to go home early today
questions.explanation: You heard 「先生、ちょっと聞いてもいいですか。」. 先生 is used to address a teacher, and 〜てもいいですか asks permission: 'may I ask you something?'

audio.text: 先生、ちょっと聞いてもいいですか。

questions.stem: Listen. Who is the speaker most likely talking to?
options: A shop assistant
A stranger
A close friend
A teacher
questions.explanation: You heard 「ねえ、明日、いっしょに買い物に行かない？」. ねえ to get attention and the plain negative question 行かない？ as an invitation are casual, used with friends and family.

audio.text: ねえ、明日、いっしょに買い物に行かない？

questions.stem: Listen. Where would you most likely hear this?
options: At a friend's front door
At the entrance of a restaurant
At a station ticket gate
In a school classroom
questions.explanation: You heard 「いらっしゃいませ。何名さまですか。」. いらっしゃいませ welcomes customers, and 何名さま politely asks how many are in the group, which is what restaurant staff ask.

audio.text: いらっしゃいませ。何名さまですか。

questions.stem: Listen. Which describes what you heard?
options: A casual question about what the listener is doing now
A casual question about what the listener did yesterday
A polite question about what the listener did yesterday
A casual question about what the listener will do tomorrow
questions.explanation: You heard 「きのうは何をしたの？」. したの is the plain past with a soft casual の, so it is casual, and きのう is yesterday. The polite version would be 何をしましたか.

audio.text: きのうは何をしたの？

questions.stem: Listen to the directions. How do you get to the library?
options: Right out of the station, left at the first lights; it's on the right
Left out of the station, right at the second lights; it's on the left
Right out of the station, right at the second lights; it's on the left
Right out of the station, left at the second lights; it's on the right
questions.explanation: You heard 「駅を出て、右に行ってください。二つ目のしんごうを左にまがると、右にとしょかんがあります」. 二つ目 is 'the second', and the と after まがる means 'when you turn'.

audio.text: 駅を出て、右に行ってください。二つ目のしんごうを左にまがると、右にとしょかんがあります。

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the department store?
options: In front of the tree
Next to the bank
In front of the bank
Behind the bank
questions.explanation: You heard 「デパートは銀行のとなりです」: となり is next to. The big tree is in front of the bank (銀行の前), a detail about a different building.

audio.text: デパートは銀行のとなりです。銀行の前に大きい木があります。

questions.stem: Listen. When does the party start?
options: Saturday at 4 pm
Saturday at 6 pm
Sunday at 6 pm
Saturday at 6 am
questions.explanation: You heard 「土曜日の午後六時から」. 土曜日 is Saturday, not 日曜日, Sunday, and 午後 is p.m.

audio.text: パーティーは土曜日の午後六時からです。場所は私の家です。

questions.stem: Listen. How much do two shirts cost?
questions.explanation: You heard 「一まい千五百円ですが、二まい買うと二千五百円です」: one costs 1,500 yen, but two cost 2,500 yen, not twice the single price.

audio.text: このシャツは一まい千五百円ですが、二まい買うと二千五百円です。

questions.stem: Listen. When is the speaker's younger sister's birthday?
options: 4 August
8 April
20 April
8 March
questions.explanation: You heard 「妹のたんじょうびは四月八日です」. 八日 is ようか, the 8th; 四月二十日 (はつか, the 20th) is the speaker's own birthday.

audio.text: 私のたんじょうびは四月二十日で、妹のたんじょうびは四月八日です。

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the Japanese.
options: 日本に二回行きたいです。
日本に二回行かなければなりません。
日本に二人で行ったことがあります。
日本に二回行ったことがあります。
questions.explanation: 'I have been to Japan twice' is experience: the た-form plus ことがあります, with 二回 for 'twice'. 二人で is 'as two people', not 'two times'.

audio.text: I have been to Japan twice.

questions.stem: Listen to the English and choose the Japanese.
options: まどをあけてください。
まどをあけましょうか。
まどをあけてみますか。
まどをあけてもいいですか。
questions.explanation: 'May I open the window?' asks permission, which is 〜てもいいですか. あけましょうか offers to do it, 'shall I open the window?', and あけてください asks someone else to.

audio.text: May I open the window?

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the Japanese.
options: 雪がふるそうです。
雪がふりました。
雪がふっています。
雪がふりそうです。
questions.explanation: 'It looks like it's going to snow' is the stem plus そうです: ふりそうです. ふるそうです, with the dictionary form, is hearsay, 'I hear it will snow'.

audio.text: It looks like it's going to snow.

questions.stem: Listen to the English sentence, then choose the Japanese.
options: おんがくを聞いても勉強しました。
おんがくを聞きながら勉強しました。
おんがくを聞いてから勉強しました。
おんがくを聞いたり勉強したりしました。
questions.explanation: 'While listening' is the stem plus ながら: 聞きながら. 聞いてから is 'after listening', and the たり form lists the two activities without saying they happened together.

audio.text: I studied while listening to music.
